content_units: Your Taste Profile at a Glance
You seem to favor   melodic, polished albums with strong songwriting  , memorable hooks, and a mix of   emotional weight + groove  . Your list points to a sweet spot between:
-   Classic songcraft   with replay value
-   Smooth, stylish production   rather than raw lo-fi edges
-   Soulful vocals   and emotionally direct performances
-   Pop/R&B/funk crossover records   that feel both accessible and musically rich
- A preference for albums that are   cohesive and refined  , not just single-heavy
Eight Album Picks Across Soul, Pop, Funk, Rock, and R&B
Artist   Album   Genre lane   Why it fits
Stevie Wonder   Songs in the Key of Life   Soul/Funk   Warm, ambitious, melodic, and packed with groove and heart
Sade   Love Deluxe   Soul/R&B   Elegant, understated, emotionally rich, and incredibly smooth
Prince   Sign o' the Times   Funk/Pop/Rock   Inventive, catchy, genre-blending, and full of rhythmic sophistication
Fleetwood Mac   Tango in the Night   Rock/Pop   A polished follow-up lane if you love the sheen and hooks of  Rumours
Solange   A Seat at the Table   Soul/R&B   Intimate, cohesive, and beautifully produced with emotional clarity
Carly Rae Jepsen   Emotion   Pop   Immaculate pop craftsmanship with big melodies and glossy production
D'Angelo   Voodoo   Soul/Funk/R&B   Deep groove, rich musicianship, and sensual, organic feel
George Michael   Listen Without Prejudice Vol. 1   Pop/Soul   Sophisticated songwriting, restraint, and adult emotional depth
Why These Match Your Listening Pattern
Your ratings suggest you respond especially well to albums with these traits:
-   High craft, low filler
Rumours ,  Back to Black , and  Continuum  all reward full-album listening rather than just standout singles.
-   Soulful but controlled vocals
Amy Winehouse, John Mayer, and Justin Timberlake all lean expressive without becoming chaotic; that points toward artists like   Sade  ,   George Michael  , and   Solange  .
-   Clean, immersive production
FutureSex/LoveSounds  and  Random Access Memories  suggest you enjoy records where production is part of the identity. That makes   Prince  ,   Stevie Wonder  , and   D'Angelo   strong fits.
-   Emotion delivered through melody

Even your slightly lower pick,  Melodrama , still signals interest in dramatic, reflective pop. You likely enjoy emotional intensity most when it's paired with strong structure and smooth replayability.
-   Genre crossover over purism
Your list jumps between rock, soul, pop, disco-funk, and R&B. So the best recommendations are albums that   blend styles confidently   rather than staying in one narrow lane.
Best First 3 to Try
Option 1:   Love Deluxe — Sade     Smooth, soulful, elegant, and likely the easiest instant match   Best for late-night listening
Listen
Option 2:   Sign o' the Times — Prince     Bold, melodic, funky, and adventurous without losing hooks   Best for range and replay
Explore
Option 3:   Emotion — Carly Rae Jepsen     Sharp, polished pop if you want more of the melodic satisfaction side   Best for pure songwriting payoff
